packet.artifact: You can deploy a static or on-demand rendered Astro site using Deno, either on your own server, or to Deno Deploy , a distributed system that runs JavaScript, TypeScript, and WebAssembly at the edge, worldwide. This guide includes instructions for running your Astro site on your own server with Deno, and deploying to Deno Deploy through GitHub Actions or the Deno Deploy CLI. Before you begin, you need the following: This guide assumes you already have Deno installed. Project Configuration Section titled “Project Configuration” Your Astro project can be deployed as a static site, or as an on-demand rendered site. Static Site Section titled “Static Site” Your Astro project is a static site by default. You don’t need any extra configuration to deploy a static Astro site with Deno, or to Deno Deploy. Adapter for on-demand rendering Section titled “Adapter for on-demand rendering” To enable on-demand rendering in your Astro project using Deno, and to deploy on Deno Deploy: Complete the following steps in order. First, Install the @deno/astro-adapter adapter to your project’s dependencies using your preferred package manager: Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them. If you are using npm: Terminal window npm install @deno/astro-adapter If you are using pnpm: Terminal window pnpm install @deno/astro-adapter If you are using yarn: Terminal window yarn add @deno/astro-adapter Second, Update your astro.config.mjs project configuration file with the changes below. astro.config.mjs import { defineConfig } from ' astro/config ' ; import deno from ' @deno/astro-adapter ' ; export default defineConfig ({ output: ' server ' , adapter: deno (), }); Finally, Update your preview script in package.json with the change below. package.json { "scripts" : { "dev" : " astro dev " , "start" : " astro dev " , "build" : " astro build " , "preview" : " astro preview " " preview " : " deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-env ./dist/server/entry.mjs " } } You can now use this command to preview your production Astro site locally with Deno. Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them. If you are using npm: Terminal window npm run preview If you are using pnpm: Terminal window pnpm run preview If you are using yarn: Terminal window yarn run preview How to deploy Section titled “How to deploy” You can run your Astro site on your own server, or deploy to Deno Deploy through GitHub Actions or using Deno Deploy’s CLI (command line interface). On your own server Section titled “On your own server” Complete the following steps in order. First, Copy your project onto your server. Second, Install the project dependencies using your preferred package manager: Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them. If you are using npm: Terminal window npm install If you are using pnpm: Terminal window pnpm install If you are using yarn: Terminal window yarn install Third, Build your Astro site with your preferred package manager: Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them. If you are using npm: Terminal window npm run build If you are using pnpm: Terminal window pnpm run build If you are using yarn: Terminal window yarn run build Finally, Start your application with the following command: Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them. If you are using static: Terminal window deno run -A jsr:@std/http/file-server dist If you are using ssr: Terminal window deno run -A ./dist/server/entry.mjs GitHub Actions Deployment Section titled “GitHub Actions Deployment” If your project is stored on GitHub, the Deno Deploy website will guide you through setting up GitHub Actions to deploy your Astro site. Complete the following steps in order. First, Push your code to a public or private GitHub repository. Second, Sign in on Deno Deploy with your GitHub account, and click on New Project . Third, Select your repository, the branch you want to deploy from, and select GitHub Action mode. (Your Astro site requires a build step, and cannot use Automatic mode.) Fourth, In your Astro project, create a new file at .github/workflows/deploy.yml and paste in the YAML below. This is similar to the YAML given by Deno Deploy, with the additional steps needed for your Astro site. Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them. If you are using static: .github/workflows/deploy.yml name : Deploy on : [ push ] jobs : deploy : name : Deploy runs-on : ubuntu-latest permissions : id-token : write # Needed for auth with Deno Deploy contents : read # Needed to clone the repository steps : - name : Clone repository uses : actions/checkout@v7 # Not using npm? Change `npm ci` to `pnpm i` or `yarn install` - name : Install dependencies run : npm ci # Not using npm? Change `npm run build` to `pnpm run build` or `yarn run build` - name : Build Astro run : npm run build - name : Upload to Deno Deploy uses : denoland/deployctl@v1 with : project : my-deno-project # TODO: replace with Deno Deploy project name entrypoint : jsr:@std/http/file-server root : dist If you are using ssr: .github/workflows/deploy.yml name : Deploy on : [ push ] jobs : deploy : name : Deploy runs-on : ubuntu-latest permissions : id-token : write # Needed for auth with Deno Deploy contents : read # Needed to clone the repository steps : - name : Clone repository uses : actions/checkout@v7 # Not using npm? Change `npm ci` to `pnpm i` or `yarn install` - name : Install dependencies run : npm ci # Not using npm? Change `npm run build` to `pnpm run build` or `yarn run build` - name : Build Astro run : npm run build - name : Upload to Deno Deploy uses : denoland/deployctl@v1 with : project : my-deno-project # TODO: replace with Deno Deploy project name entrypoint : dist/server/entry.mjs Finally, After committing this YAML file, and pushing to GitHub on your configured deploy branch, the deploy should begin automatically! You can track the progress using the “Actions” tab on your GitHub repository page, or on Deno Deploy . CLI Deployment Section titled “CLI Deployment” Complete the following steps in order. First, Install the Deno Deploy CLI . Terminal window deno install -gArf jsr:@deno/deployctl Second, Build your Astro site with your preferred package manager: Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them. If you are using npm: Terminal window npm run build If you are using pnpm: Terminal window pnpm run build If you are using yarn: Terminal window yarn run build Third, Run deployctl to deploy! Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them. If you are using static: Terminal window cd dist && deployctl deploy jsr:@std/http/file-server If you are using ssr: Terminal window deployctl deploy ./dist/server/entry.mjs You can track all your deploys on Deno Deploy . Finally, (Optional) To simplify the build and deploy into one command, add a deploy-deno script in package.json , adapting it for your preferred package manager. Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them. If you are using static: package.json { "scripts" : { "dev" : " astro dev " , "start" : " astro dev " , "build" : " astro build " , "preview" : " astro preview " , "deno-deploy" : " npm run build && cd dist && deployctl deploy jsr:@std/http/file-server " } } If you are using ssr: package.json { "scripts" : { "dev" : " astro dev " , "start" : " astro dev " , "build" : " astro build " , "preview" : " deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-env ./dist/server/entry.mjs " , "deno-deploy" : " npm run build && deployctl deploy ./dist/server/entry.mjs " } } Then you can use this command to build and deploy your Astro site in one step. Choose one of the following options. These are alternatives — use exactly one, not all of them. If you are using npm: Terminal window npm run deno-deploy If you are using pnpm: Terminal window pnpm run deno-deploy If you are using yarn: Terminal window yarn run deno-deploy More Deployment Guides AWS AWS via Flightcontrol AWS via SST Azion Buddy Cleavr Clever Cloud Cloudflare CloudRay Deno Deploy DeployHQ EdgeOne Pages Firebase Fleek Fly.io GitHub Pages GitLab Pages Google Cloud Heroku Hostinger Microsoft Azure Netlify Railway Render Seenode Sevalla Stormkit Surge Vercel Zeabur Zephyr Cloud Zerops Recipes
